stats: of 300 places I checked close on Sundays
the most common break between lunch and dinner

slides.en:
One in three
close on Sunday
facts: Plan Sunday around places open every day
Save the tiny shops for weekdays

slides.body: Many kitchens close between lunch and dinner.
slides.badge: 92 of 300 take a break · most often 3–5pm
facts: Use 3–5pm for coffee, sweets or a temple

slides.en:
Closing time is
not last order
slides.body: Kitchens stop taking orders before the door closes.
slides.badge: 108 list a last order · usually 30–60 min before
facts: Arrive at least an hour before closing
まだ大丈夫ですか？ mada daijōbu desu ka? = still OK?

slides.body: Cheap, old and tiny places most of all.
facts: Get yen at a convenience-store ATM before lunch
Keep coins and ¥1,000 notes for ticket machines

slides.body: At many izakaya a small starter arrives unasked. It's a table charge, not a scam.
facts: Check the menu or ask before you sit down
Some places add a night-time service charge too

slides.body: The bill comes to your table; you take it to the register by the door.
facts: お会計お願いします okaikei onegaishimasu = the check, please

slides.body: Leave money behind and staff may run after you to return it.
facts: ごちそうさまでした gochisōsama deshita = thank you for the meal

slides.body: Staff won't hover. Raise your hand and say it out loud.
facts: すみません！ sumimasen = excuse me!
Many tables have a call button

lines: Otōshi · pay at the register · no tips · すみません
